commit.message:
Show a dbt Core style execution index on node result lines

* Show a dbt Core style execution index on node result lines

dbt Core prefixes every per-node progress log with an execution index
("1 of 53 OK created ..."), which users rely on to gauge how far a run
has gotten. Fusion had no equivalent.

Add `node_index` / `node_count_total` to the `NodeProcessed` event and
render them inside the existing duration bracket, so a result line now
reads:

  Succeeded [ 3 of 53 in   0.34s] model analytics.fct_orders (table)

The index is claimed inside the `NodeProcessed` span builder, which the
span manager invokes lazily and exactly once as a node's first task
opens. That makes the number reflect the order nodes begin processing,
which is what dbt Core's dequeue counter measures, and needs no
scheduler changes. Ephemeral models are excluded from both the index and
the denominator: Fusion pulls them into the selection to build them and
reports them as no-op skips that never print, so counting them would
leave the largest index short of the total. dbt Core leaves them out for
the same reason.

The counter is right-aligned to the width of the total so the columns
after the bracket hold their position. Rows with no meaningful elapsed
time render the duration as dashes, and "in -------" reads wrong, so
those get padding where "in" would go, keeping the bracket width
identical. Grouped lines (the skipped-test summary and aggregated
generic-test headers) stand in for several nodes and so show no index,
but pad to the same width to stay aligned.

All three sinks carry it: stdout, logs/dbt.log, and --log-format json.
The JSON payloads gain `index` and `total` as structured fields, using
dbt Core's field names and its convention of emitting 0 for ephemeral
models. This resolves a standing TODO in the json compat layer.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Move the execution index to the end of node result lines

Feedback on the first cut: putting the counter in the middle of the line
pushed the columns after it around and buried the information users
actually scan for. Move it to the end instead, where it reads as an
annotation on the line rather than a column in it.

  Succeeded seed  main.raw_orders (table) [1 of 11 in 0.02s]
     Passed test  not_null_fct_orders_amount [7 of 11 in 0.01s]
    Skipped model main.child_of_broken (view) [11 of 11]

The action keeps its right-aligned column, so it still lines up with
every other progress message ("Loading", "Parsing", "Installing").

Because the field no longer sits mid-line, nothing downstream depends on
its width, so the counter and the duration render at their natural size
instead of being padded to fixed widths. Two consequences:

- A zero duration is dropped rather than printed as `-------`, since
  skips and cache reuse have nothing to time.
- When there is neither a counter nor an elapsed time, the brackets are
  omitted altogether rather than emitted empty. This is what the grouped
  skipped-test summary hits.

Grouped lines (that summary and aggregated generic-test headers) stand in
for several nodes, so they report elapsed time alone.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Update golden files for the execution index

Applied from the CI patches for run 33114625062 via
`cargo xtask apply-ci-goldies` (348 patch blocks, all validated with
`git apply --check` first). These cover the warehouse-backed goldies
(Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks) that cannot be regenerated locally.

Text goldies move the trailing field into place:

  - Succeeded [duration] model pub.stg_payments (view)
  + Succeeded model pub.stg_payments (view) [1 of 8 in duration]

Nodes with nothing to time lose the placeholder duration entirely:

  + Succeeded seed  pub.raw_orders (table) [2 of 8]

JSONL/OTLP telemetry goldies pick up the new `node_index` and
`node_count_total` span attributes.

Lines that intentionally carry no counter, and so change only by losing
their duration bracket: ephemeral models (excluded from the numbering, as
in dbt Core), aggregated generic-test group headers (they stand for
several nodes), and source freshness results (sources are partitioned out
of the scheduler's selected set, so they are not numbered today).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Update goldens for the execution index after merging main

Applied from the CI run's golden patches: node result lines pick up the
trailing [N of M in duration] field, and the otel snapshots gain the
node_index / node_count_total span attributes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Update two goldens for zero-duration execution index fields

Both nodes fail before any execution is timed, so the progress field
renders as a bare [N of M] with no elapsed time.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Decide the elapsed field from the outcome, not from a zero duration

The progress field read a zero duration as "nothing to time" and dropped
the elapsed part. But duration_ms counts whole milliseconds, so a node
that really did run can measure zero: any node near the 0/1ms boundary
rendered [N of M] on one run and [N of M in 0.00s] on the next, and its
golden flapped with it. Two goldens flipped between consecutive CI runs
on this branch, and eight more were sitting on the same boundary.

The caller already knows which work never ran -- it is the same condition
that used to zero the duration -- so pass that through as Option and let a
measured zero render like any other measurement.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Reconcile two goldens with node counts that changed on main

The merge queue tests this branch against current main, and two goldens
came out of the merge in a state the binary can never produce.

`adapters_snowflake_repros_snapshot_warning_1` gained a fourth snapshot
on main. Git merged that line in from main's side, in the pre-index
format, while keeping this branch's three indexed lines that were
recorded when the project only had three snapshots. The result claimed
`[1 of 3]` through `[3 of 3]` alongside an un-indexed fourth node, with
a summary reporting four. All four lines now carry `[N of 4]`.

`run_lake_compute_seed_build_demo` is new on main and was recorded
before this branch existed, so every result line was still in the
pre-index format. Its counter values come from running the test locally
-- it replays a recording, so it needs no warehouse. Only the eight
result lines are touched: the local run also drops the stderr warnings
and the execution summary and reports dbt State as enabled, none of
which reproduce in CI, so accepting the generated golden wholesale
would have baked local environment state into it.

The 126 goldens still showing the pre-index format are not stale. They
cover node kinds that take no index, `check` nodes chief among them, and
they pass on this branch's own CI run.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Stop pinning the execution index in tests that sort their output

`run_lake_compute_seed_build_demo` failed CI on every retry, each time
wanting different numbers. Three retries in one job disagreed with each
other: `unique_raw_customers_customer_id` came back as 3, then 2, then
4, and five of the eight nodes moved. No golden value can be chosen that
survives the next run.

The test runs `fs_vec_par(.., Some(0))`, so Fusion schedules its nodes
concurrently and the order they start in -- which is the order the index
is handed out in -- differs run to run. It passed on main only because
main's golden predates the index.

Sorting is already how a test declares that its node order is not fixed,
so that flag is exactly the right condition: normalize the position for
tests that sort, leave it asserted for tests that do not. Sequential
tests keep full coverage of the numbering, which is where the numbering
is meaningful in the first place.

The total is deliberately left alone. It is stable regardless of
scheduling, and it is what catches a node entering or leaving the
selection -- the failure this branch hit when a snapshot was added on
main.

Normalizing both sides of the comparison means no existing golden had to
change. The eight lake_compute goldens updated here only swap pinned
numbers for `index`, matching what `--goldie-update` now writes, so they
no longer read as though a position were being asserted.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
